knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Column Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form inequality systems with explicit nonnegative slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax+s=b\) with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(s\ge 0\), a slack-column basis is a selection of \(m\) linearly independent columns that includes columns from the slack-variable block \(I_m\). Selecting all \(m\) slack columns gives \(B=I_m\), nonbasic structural variables \(x=0\), and basic values \(s=b\). The all-slack basis is primal feasible exactly when \(b\ge 0\) componentwise; a partly slack-based selection is primal feasible exactly when its induced basic solution satisfies all sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slack-column basis is a nonsingular column selection containing slack-variable identity columns. The all-slack basis is the identity basis and is primal feasible exactly when the right-hand side is componentwise nonnegative; a partly slack-based basis requires a separate feasibility check.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and the inequalities are written as \(Ax+s=b\) with \(s\ge 0\).
The selected slack columns correspond to distinct constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A partly slack-based selection is a basis exactly when its selected matrix \(B\) is nonsingular; selecting every slack column gives \(B=I_m\) and a primal-feasible start exactly when \(b\ge 0\) componentwise.

children.title: Explicit-Bound Bases
children.top_down_role: Basis starts organized around explicit variable-bound statuses.

assumptions_latex: A bounded-variable linear program has finite bounds represented by additional equality rows and nonnegative bound slacks.
The chosen bound columns are linearly independent and their number completes a square basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chosen explicit-bound columns constitute a basis whose basic solution fixes associated variables at their represented bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds are represented explicitly by equality rows and slack variables.

source_refs.locator: Bases and Vertices p. 32

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose finite bounds are expressed by equations \(x_i-v_i=\ell_i\) or \(x_i+w_i=u_i\), where \(v_i,w_i\ge 0\). An explicit-bound basis is a nonsingular square column selection containing columns from these bound equations, so that the associated nonbasic bound slacks are set to zero and the corresponding variables satisfy \(x_i=\ell_i\) or \(x_i=u_i\). It is an admissible starting basis only when the complete induced basic solution satisfies every sign and bound restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit-bound basis uses columns from equations representing finite variable bounds. Setting the associated bound slacks to zero places variables at bounds, subject to feasibility of the full basic solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-Bound Bases

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed start combines ordinary slack columns and bound-equation columns. It is usable when the selected matrix is nonsingular and the induced basic solution satisfies all signs and bounds.

children.title: Identity Bases
children.top_down_role: Basis starts obtained from identity-like submatrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Identity Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unit-column structures in an equality-form linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Mz=d\) with \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), an identity basis is a selection of \(m\) columns whose basis matrix satisfies \(B=I_m\), or more generally \(B=P\) for a permutation matrix \(P\). After the complementary nonbasic variables are fixed at values \(z_N\), the basic vector is \(z_B=B^{-1}(d-M_Nz_N)=P^{\mathsf T}(d-M_Nz_N)\). Thus nonsingularity and the basis solve are immediate; primal feasibility still requires \(z_B\) and \(z_N\) to satisfy their sign and bound restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identity basis contains one unit column for each row, possibly reordered. After accounting for the fixed nonbasic variables, its basic values are obtained by permuting the residual right-hand side; feasibility still requires all variable restrictions to hold.
assumptions_latex: The equality-form system is \(Mz=d\), where \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) contains \(m\) columns equal to distinct unit vectors.
The chosen unit columns cover every row exactly once, and the complementary variables have fixed values \(z_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis matrix is a column permutation \(P\) of \(I_m\), and \(z_B=P^{\mathsf T}(d-M_Nz_N)\) is obtained without matrix factorization.

knowledge_statements.title: Triangular Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bases triangular after row and column permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A triangular basis is a column selection for which permutation matrices \(P\) and \(Q\) give \(T=PBQ\), with \(T\) upper or lower triangular. The selection is a valid basis if and only if \(T_{ii}\ne 0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\), equivalently \(\det(B)\ne 0\). For a right-hand side \(d\), the basic vector is computed by one triangular substitution followed by undoing the permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A triangular basis becomes triangular after row and column permutations. It is nonsingular exactly when every diagonal entry is nonzero, and its basic values follow by triangular substitution.
assumptions_latex: A selection of \(m\) columns yields a matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\).
Some row and column permutations make \(B\) triangular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selection is a basis exactly when every diagonal entry of the permuted triangular matrix is nonzero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block-organized basis admits permutations satisfying \(PBQ=\operatorname{diag}(B_{11},\ldots,B_{rr})\), or a block upper or lower triangular analogue. It is nonsingular exactly when every diagonal block \(B_{kk}\) is nonsingular. Consequently, solving \(Bz_B=d\) decomposes into independent block solves in the diagonal case and into ordered block substitution in the triangular case; primal feasibility is then checked on the assembled \(z_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-organized basis is block diagonal or block triangular after permutations. Nonsingular diagonal blocks yield a valid basis and permit independent or ordered block solves.

assumptions_latex: A candidate column set \(J\) has cardinality equal to the row rank \(m\) of \(M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Mz=d\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=m\), a structural selection \(J\) is basis-compatible when \(|J|=m\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(M_J)=m\). After admissible nonbasic values \(z_N\) are fixed, it induces \(z_J=M_J^{-1}(d-M_Nz_N)\). The selection is compatible with an immediate primal start precisely when this vector satisfies every sign and bound restriction assigned to the basic variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural compatibility requires a full-rank square column selection. With admissible nonbasic values fixed, it becomes an immediate primal start only if all computed basic values are admissible.

children.title: Crash-Basis Construction Interface
children.top_down_role: Logical, structural-matching, and rank-revealing crash families, with implementation details delegated to solver architecture.

assumptions_latex: The equality-form matrix \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
A crash routine may inspect sparsity, coefficients, bounds, and row-column incidence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns either a nonsingular basis index set or an explicit failure status requiring a general initialization method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract solver-facing contract, independent of a particular crash heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \((M,d,\ell,u)\). Construct a candidate set \(J\) of \(m\) columns using structural matching, logical-column preference, or rank-revealing selection. Test \(\operatorname{rank}(M_J)=m\); if it fails, revise \(J\) or return failure. Otherwise assign admissible nonbasic values \(z_N\), solve \(M_Jz_J=d-M_Nz_N\), and report \((J,z)\) together with primal-feasibility and bound-violation indicators. Output a starting basis only after nonsingularity has been established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A crash interface selects structurally promising columns, verifies full rank, computes the induced basic solution, and returns the basis with feasibility diagnostics or an explicit failure status.

children.title: Two-Phase Simplex Method
children.top_down_role: The classical separation of feasibility acquisition from optimization of the original objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete two-phase simplex method and outcome guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form two-phase simplex, including artificial-basis cleanup and its outcomes when cycling is avoided.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), first change row signs so that \(b\ge0\). Phase I introduces artificial variables and minimizes their sum. A positive Phase-I optimum proves infeasibility. At value zero, artificial basics are pivoted out using eligible original columns, while a row with no eligible original-column entry is deleted as redundant. Phase II starts from the resulting feasible basis, recomputes reduced costs using \(c\), and applies simplex to the original objective. If cycling is avoided, Phase I either detects infeasibility or produces a feasible basis after any necessary redundant-row deletions; Phase II then either detects unboundedness below or terminates with an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I minimizes artificial variables to test feasibility and construct a usable basis, deleting redundant equalities when necessary. Phase II restores the original costs and runs simplex from that basis. When cycling is avoided, the method detects infeasibility or unboundedness, or returns an optimal solution; redundant-row deletion is an intermediate correction rather than a mutually exclusive terminal outcome.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb R^m,\quad x\ge0
\text{Row signs are normalized so that }b\ge0.
\text{Cycling is avoided.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm I}>0\Rightarrow\text{infeasibility};\quad v_{\mathrm I}=0\Rightarrow\text{a feasible Phase-II basis after any required row cleanup};\quad\text{Phase II detects unboundedness below or returns an optimum}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Phase Simplex Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical initialization with one nonnegative artificial variable per equality row; zero-valued artificial basic variables may require pivoting or redundant-row removal before Phase II.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), introduce \(x_a\geq0\) and solve Phase I: \(\min\{\mathbf1^Tx_a:Ax+x_a=b,\ x,x_a\geq0\}\), initialized at \(x=0\) and \(x_a=b\). If the Phase-I optimum is positive, declare the original system infeasible. If it is zero, retain the resulting feasible original-variable solution, pivot out any zero-valued artificial basic variables when possible, remove any rows thereby shown redundant, and then optimize the original objective in Phase II.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the sum of nonnegative artificial variables to acquire primal feasibility. A positive Phase-I optimum certifies infeasibility. A zero optimum gives a feasible original-variable solution, but zero-valued artificial variables may remain basic; they must be pivoted out, or associated redundant rows removed, before handing an appropriate basis to Phase II.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb R_+^m,\quad c\in\mathbb R^n
Ax=b,\quad x\geq0
Ax+x_a=b,\quad x\geq0,\quad x_a\geq0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{\mathbf1^Tx_a:Ax+x_a=b,\ x,x_a\geq0\}>0\Rightarrow\{x\geq0:Ax=b\}=\varnothing;\quad \min=0\Rightarrow\text{a feasible original-variable solution exists and Phase II follows the necessary artificial-basis cleanup.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(r\in R\), append a nonnegative artificial variable \(a_r\) with a unit column in row \(r\), choosing row signs so the initial artificial values are nonnegative. Solve Phase I: \(\min\{\sum_{r\in R}a_r: Ax+Ea=b,\ x\ge0,\ a\ge0\}\). Stop at an optimum. If its value is positive, declare the original system infeasible; if it is zero, remove the artificial variables after obtaining a valid original-variable basis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiple-artificial-variable Phase I and feasible-basis handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical two-phase simplex initialization for a nonnegative equality-form LP, using one artificial variable per row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the feasibility system \(Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\), first change row signs as necessary so that \(b_i\ge 0\). Introduce \(a\in\mathbb R_+^M\) with \(Ax+a=b\), take \(a=b\) as the initial artificial basis, and solve \(\min w=\mathbf 1^Ta\) by simplex. If \(w^*>0\), terminate because the original system is infeasible. If \(w^*=0\), remove from further consideration each nonbasic original variable whose coefficient in the final modified \(w\)-row is strictly positive, delete the Phase-I objective, eliminate the current basic variables from the original objective row, and pass the resulting feasible canonical basis to Phase II.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Make every right-hand side nonnegative, add one nonnegative artificial variable per equation, and minimize their sum from the artificial basis. A positive Phase-I optimum certifies infeasibility. At a zero optimum, remove the Phase-I objective and the specified unusable nonbasic columns, restore the original objective row, and hand the feasible basis to Phase II.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{M\times N},\quad b\in\mathbb R^M,\quad x\in\mathbb R_+^N
b_i\ge 0\quad(i=1,\ldots,M)\text{ after permissible row sign changes}
Ax+a=b,\quad a\in\mathbb R_+^M,\quad w=\mathbf 1^Ta
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^*>0\Rightarrow\{x\ge 0:Ax=b\}=\varnothing;\qquad w^*=0\Rightarrow\text{a feasible-basis handoff to Phase II is available}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Phase-I tableau pivot and termination rules with multiple artificial variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase-I portion of the classical two-phase tableau simplex method using one artificial variable per equality row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible Phase-I canonical tableau, let \(d_j\) denote the Phase-I reduced-cost entries and \(\bar w_0\) the current value of \(w\). If \(d_j\ge 0\) for every eligible column, terminate Phase I: \(\bar w_0>0\) certifies infeasibility, whereas \(\bar w_0=0\) triggers deletion of columns with \(d_j>0\), removal of the \(w\)-row, and handoff to Phase II. If some \(d_j<0\), choose \(s\) with \(d_s=\min_j d_j\). In Phase I the case \(\bar a_{is}\le 0\) for all \(i\) cannot occur. Hence choose a leaving row \(r\) satisfying \[\frac{\bar b_r}{\bar a_{rs}}=\min_{i:\,\bar a_{is}>0}\frac{\bar b_i}{\bar a_{is}},\] selecting uniformly at random among tied rows, and perform the Gauss--Jordan pivot on \(\bar a_{rs}\) to obtain the next feasible tableau.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In Phase I, nonnegative reduced costs end the phase: a positive artificial objective proves infeasibility, while zero initiates the Phase-II handoff. Otherwise enter a column of minimum reduced cost, apply the minimum-ratio test over its positive entries, choose uniformly among ties, and pivot. The no-positive-entry unbounded branch cannot occur in Phase I.
assumptions_latex: \bar b_i\ge 0\quad(i=1,\ldots,M)
\text{the current Phase-I tableau is in feasible canonical form}
w=\sum_{i=1}^M a_i,\quad a_i\ge 0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each Phase-I cycle either certifies infeasibility, hands a feasible basis to Phase II, or produces the next feasible tableau by a ratio-test pivot.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Artificial-variable Phase-I feasibility problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form LP feasibility initialization using one artificial variable per equality, including the direct handoff case in which the final basis contains only original columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), change row signs so that \(b\ge0\), then solve \(\min\{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}y:Ax+y=b,\ x\ge0,\ y\ge0\}\), initialized at \((x,y)=(0,b)\). The original constraints are feasible if and only if the auxiliary optimum is zero; a positive auxiliary optimum proves infeasibility. At auxiliary value zero, \(y=0\) and \(x\) is feasible for the original problem. If the final auxiliary basis consists entirely of columns of \(A\), the artificial columns may be deleted and that basis used to initialize simplex on the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After making the right-hand side nonnegative, add nonnegative artificial variables and minimize their sum from the identity basis. The auxiliary optimum is zero exactly when the original constraints are feasible and is positive otherwise. If the zero-optimum basis uses only original columns, it directly initializes simplex for the original problem.

\text{Row signs have been chosen so that }b\ge0.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Artificial-Variable Phase I
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-artificial-variable Phase I; the auxiliary column depends on the chosen construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an auxiliary column \(q\in\mathbb{R}^m\) so that \(Ax+qt=b\), \(x\ge 0\), \(t\ge 0\), has an explicitly available initial basic feasible solution. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the augmented minimization objective as \(M\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}a+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(M\) is a formal positive symbol larger than every real scalar. Compare affine expressions \(M\alpha+\beta\) and \(M\alpha'+\beta'\) by first comparing \(\alpha\) with \(\alpha'\), and only when they are equal comparing \(\beta\) with \(\beta'\). Thus symbolic Big-M simplex first minimizes the total artificial-variable value and, among points attaining its minimum, minimizes the original objective. No finite numerical value is assigned to \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Formal Big-M arithmetic orders solutions first by total artificial value and then by the original objective, without selecting a numerical penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(x\ge0\) and \(a\ge0\).
Objective expressions are affine in the formal symbol \(M\).
All comparisons use the infinite-priority ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing \(M\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}a+c^{\mathsf T}x\) is hierarchical minimization of \(\bigl(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}a,c^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Big-M Priorities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-pair formulation of the artificial-first Big-M objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each feasible augmented point the objective pair \(\bigl(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}a,c^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\in\mathbb R^2\). Order pairs lexicographically: \((u,v)<_{\mathrm{lex}}(u',v')\) exactly when \(u<u'\), or when \(u=u'\) and \(v<v'\). Tableau costs and reduced costs are propagated componentwise as ordered pairs. A lexicographic minimizer therefore minimizes artificial infeasibility first and uses the original cost only to distinguish solutions with the same artificial objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered cost pairs encode Big-M priority by minimizing artificial infeasibility first and the original cost second.
assumptions_latex: The augmented feasible set is nonempty.
Both objective components are finite at the compared points.
Pair comparisons use \(<_{\mathrm{lex}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective is \(\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\bigl(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}a,c^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of formal affine Big-M costs and lexicographically ordered cost pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(M)=M\alpha+\beta\) and associate it with \(T(\phi)=(\alpha,\beta)\). Under the formal ordering in which \(M\) dominates every real constant, \(\phi(M)<\psi(M)\) if and only if \(T(\phi)<_{\mathrm{lex}}T(\psi)\). Hence symbolic Big-M and ordered-pair simplex produce identical reduced-cost signs and priority comparisons. If both implementations also use the same deterministic rules for every entering-variable, leaving-variable, and zero-cost tie, they generate the same pivot sequence and terminal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine symbolic Big-M expressions and lexicographic coefficient pairs have identical order; matching tie rules then give the same simplex pivots and basis.
assumptions_latex: All compared expressions have degree at most one in \(M\).
\(M\) has infinite priority over real constants.
Both algorithms use identical deterministic tie rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\alpha+\beta<M\alpha'+\beta'\iff(\alpha,\beta)<_{\mathrm{lex}}(\alpha',\beta')\), with identical pivots under common tie-breaking.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Priority Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-level divergence caused by unresolved simplex ties despite equivalent priority representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Priority-representation equivalence determines the ordering of distinct affine objective values but does not select among tied pivots. If a tableau has multiple eligible entering variables with the same ordered reduced cost, multiple leaving variables attaining the same minimum ratio, or a zero-length degenerate pivot, symbolic and pair-valued implementations may choose different adjacent bases when their tie rules differ. They still preserve the same hierarchical objective ordering and may represent the same primal point. Divergence is excluded when all relevant comparisons are strict or a common deterministic tie rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent Big-M priorities can follow different degenerate bases when pivot ties are resolved differently, although their hierarchical objective ordering remains identical.
assumptions_latex: Symbolic and pair representations encode the same affine costs.
At least one entering, ratio, or degenerate pivot tie occurs.
The implementations use different tie rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Priority equivalence alone does not imply equality of pivot sequences or terminal bases under degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Penalty Big-M
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-penalty threshold ensuring that every augmented optimum eliminates artificial variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its augmented problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+M\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}a:Ax+a=b,\ x,a\ge0\}\). Suppose the original problem has an optimal dual multiplier \(y^*\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y^*\le c\). If \(M>\max_i y_i^*\), then \(y^*\) is feasible for the augmented dual with every artificial-variable dual inequality strict. Consequently every augmented optimal solution has \(a=0\) and its \(x\)-component solves the original problem. Equality at the threshold need not exclude optimal solutions with positive artificial components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite penalty strictly exceeding every component of an optimal original dual multiplier forces all artificial variables to zero at every augmented optimum.
assumptions_latex: The original primal and dual have attained finite optima.
The augmented problem is feasible.
Artificial columns form \(I\) and have common cost \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M>\max_i y_i^*\) implies \(a=0\) for every augmented optimum and preserves the original optimal value.

notation.meaning: optimal dual multiplier of the original problem

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Phase-I Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary optimization for acquiring a dual-feasible multiplier before dual-simplex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal standard-form problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), dual feasibility requires \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\) with \(s\ge0\). Solve the always-feasible auxiliary problem \(\min \mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}u\) subject to \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s-u=c\), \(s,u\ge0\), with \(y\) free. If its optimum is zero, output an optimal \(y\) and \(s\); they form a dual-feasible starting point for a dual-oriented simplex procedure. If the optimum is positive, report that the dual-feasibility system has no solution and do not begin the optimization phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize explicit violations of the dual inequalities; zero violation supplies a dual-feasible start, while a positive optimum shows dual feasibility is impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The auxiliary LP is solved to an attained optimum.
\(y\) is unrestricted in sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The auxiliary optimum is \(0\) if and only if some \((y,s)\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\) and \(s\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual simplex method for a canonical minimization problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinary dual-simplex iteration for canonical-form minimization problems, excluding the bounded-variable specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a basis \(B\) satisfying \(z_j-c_j=c_BB^{-1}a_j-c_j\le 0\) for every \(j\). At each iteration compute \(\bar b=B^{-1}b\). If \(\bar b\ge 0\), stop: the current solution is optimal. Otherwise choose a row \(r\) with \(\bar b_r<0\), for example one satisfying \(\bar b_r=\min_i\bar b_i\). If \(y_{rj}\ge 0\) for every \(j\), stop: the dual is unbounded and the primal is infeasible. Otherwise choose \(k\) such that \[\frac{z_k-c_k}{y_{rk}}=\min_{j:y_{rj}<0}\frac{z_j-c_j}{y_{rj}},\] pivot on \(y_{rk}\), and repeat.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Simplex Method in Matrix-Dictionary Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A dual-feasible simplex iteration that maintains dual feasibility and complementarity while seeking primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume a basis \(\mathcal B\), nonbasis \(\mathcal N\), and a dual-feasible dictionary with \(z_{\mathcal N}^*\ge 0\). If \(x_{\mathcal B}^*\ge 0\), stop: the current solution is optimal. Otherwise choose \(i\in\mathcal B\) with \(x_i^*<0\), compute \(\Delta z_{\mathcal N}=-(B^{-1}N)^T e_i\), and set \(s=\left(\max_{j\in\mathcal N}\Delta z_j/z_j^*\right)^{-1}\). If \(s\) is not positive, stop: the dual is unbounded, implying that the primal is infeasible. Otherwise choose any maximizing \(j\in\mathcal N\), compute \(\Delta x_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}Ne_j\) and \(t=x_i^*/\Delta x_i\), update \(x_j^*\leftarrow t\), \(x_{\mathcal B}^*\leftarrow x_{\mathcal B}^*-t\Delta x_{\mathcal B}\), \(z_i^*\leftarrow s\), and \(z_{\mathcal N}^*\leftarrow z_{\mathcal N}^*-s\Delta z_{\mathcal N}\), and replace \(\mathcal B\) by \((\mathcal B\setminus\{i\})\cup\{j\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a dual-feasible dictionary, the dual simplex method stops as optimal once the basic primal variables are nonnegative. Otherwise it selects a negative basic primal variable, computes the dual direction and ratio step, and declares the dual unbounded—and the primal infeasible—if the resulting step is not positive. For a positive step, it selects a maximizing nonbasic index, computes the corresponding primal direction and step, updates the dictionary, and pivots the basis. Dual feasibility and complementarity are maintained until primal feasibility is attained.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ is the current basis matrix with basic index set }\mathcal B\text{ and nonbasic index set }\mathcal N.
z_{\mathcal N}^*\ge 0
\text{The current primal--dual dictionary satisfies complementarity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Simplex Pivot Rule and Primal-Infeasibility Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau-form dual-simplex iteration under the sign convention that nonnegative reduced costs express dual feasibility and nonnegative basic values express primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) for every nonbasic index \(j\). If \(\bar b_i\ge 0\) for every basic index \(i\), stop: the associated basic solution is primal feasible and optimal. Otherwise choose a leaving row \(r\) with \(\bar b_r=\min_i\bar b_i<0\). If \(\bar a_{rj}\ge 0\) for every nonbasic index \(j\), conclude that the primal problem is infeasible. Otherwise choose an entering column \(s\) satisfying \[\frac{\bar c_s}{-\bar a_{rs}}=\min_{j:\,\bar a_{rj}<0}\frac{\bar c_j}{-\bar a_{rj}},\] and pivot on \((r,s)\). Thus the leaving basic variable is selected before the entering nonbasic variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain dual feasibility by keeping all nonbasic reduced costs nonnegative. If all basic values are nonnegative, the current basic solution is feasible and optimal. Otherwise choose a row with minimum, negative basic value. If that row has no negative coefficient in a nonbasic column, the primal problem is infeasible. Otherwise enter a column minimizing the ratio of its reduced cost to the negative pivot-row coefficient, then pivot. The leaving variable is therefore selected before the entering variable.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) for every nonbasic index \(j\) in the current tableau.
The tableau sign convention identifies \(\bar b_i\ge 0\) with primal feasibility and \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) with dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\forall i,\ \bar b_i\ge0\bigr)\Rightarrow\text{optimality};\quad \bigl(\bar b_r<0\land\forall j,\ \bar a_{rj}\ge0\bigr)\Rightarrow\text{primal infeasibility};\) otherwise pivot according to the stated minimum-ratio rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Primal-Dual Basis Frameworks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents complementary primal and dual states through one common basis partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in\mathbb R^n_+\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ y\in\mathbb R^m,\ s\in\mathbb R^n_+\}\), a complementary basis framework chooses a partition \(B\mathbin{\dot\cup}N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that \(A_B\) is nonsingular, and sets \(x_N=0\) and \(s_B=0\). It then determines \[x_B=A_B^{-1}b,\qquad y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\qquad s_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y.\] Consequently, \(x_i s_i=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). If additionally \(x_B\ge0\) and \(s_N\ge0\), the displayed primal and dual solutions are feasible and have equal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a standard-form primal-dual pair, one nonsingular basis partition sets the nonbasic primal variables and basic dual slacks to zero, thereby enforcing complementarity. If the remaining primal variables and dual slacks are nonnegative, the two solutions are feasible and optimal with equal objective values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criss-cross pivots and least-index anti-cycling rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criss-cross tableau pivots from an arbitrary nonsingular basis, without maintaining primal or dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_B=p+Qx_N\), \(z=z_0+r^Tx_N\) with \(A_B\) nonsingular, a primal pivot chooses \(r_\beta>0\) and \(q_{\alpha\beta}<0\), while a dual pivot chooses \(p_\alpha<0\) and \(q_{\alpha\beta}>0\); neither requires the feasibility-preserving ratio test of the corresponding simplex orientation. In either case, \(B'=(B\setminus\{k_\alpha\})\cup\{\ell_\beta\}\) is a basis. If the LP has an optimal solution, every basis either has \(p\ge0\) and \(r\le0\), hence induces an optimal basic feasible solution, or admits a primal or dual pivot. Arbitrary choices can cycle even without degeneracy. Define \(\alpha^*=\min\{\alpha:\exists\beta,\ r_\beta>0,\ q_{\alpha\beta}<0\}\) and \(\beta^*=\min\{\beta:\exists\alpha,\ p_\alpha<0,\ q_{\alpha\beta}>0\}\). Choosing the primal step with \(\alpha=\alpha^*\) and least possible \(\beta\) when \(\alpha^*\le\beta^*\), and otherwise the dual step with \(\beta=\beta^*\) and least possible \(\alpha\), is noncycling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Criss-cross starts from any nonsingular basis and alternates between primal and dual pivots without preserving either feasibility invariant. When an optimum exists, a basis is either already primal and dual feasible or admits one of the two pivots. Unrestricted choices may cycle even on a nondegenerate problem, but the stated least-index rule does not cycle.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A tableau boundary at which dual-simplex recovery certifies primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), with basis \(B\). If some basic row \(r\) satisfies \((B^{-1}b)_r<0\) and \((B^{-1}A_N)_{rj}\ge0\) for every nonbasic index \(j\), then no nonbasic variable can enter through that row to restore its feasibility. With \(u^T=e_r^TB^{-1}\), one has \(u^TA\ge0\) and \(u^Tb<0\). Thus \(u\) is a directly checkable Farkas certificate that \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an infeasible basic row has no coefficient permitting a dual-simplex pivot, that row yields a Farkas certificate of primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an invertible basis submatrix of \(A\).
All nonbasic variables are fixed at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(u^TA\ge0\) and \(u^Tb<0\) certify that no \(x\ge0\) satisfies \(Ax=b\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal bounded-variable simplex with nonbasic variables fixed at finite lower or upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(l\le x\le u\), partition indices into basic, lower-nonbasic, and upper-nonbasic sets. Fix \(x_L=l_L\) and \(x_U=u_U\), then compute \(x_B=B^{-1}(b-A_Ll_L-A_Uu_U)\). Maintain \(l_B\le x_B\le u_B\). With \(y=B^{-T}c_B\) and \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^Ty\), optimality holds when \(\bar c_j\ge0\) at every lower bound and \(\bar c_j\le0\) at every upper bound. Otherwise select a violating nonbasic variable and move it toward its opposite bound. If a basic variable reaches a bound first, pivot there; if the moving variable reaches its opposite bound first, change its nonbasic bound status without a basis pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonbasic variables sit at lower or upper bounds; a reduced-cost violator moves until a basic variable reaches a bound and pivots, or until the violator reaches its opposite bound and flips status.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
\(l_i<u_i\), allowing infinite endpoints where the corresponding bound status is unavailable.
An initial bound-feasible basis-status assignment is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the sign conditions on all nonbasic reduced costs hold, the current bounded basic feasible solution is optimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-variable simplex terminates if every iteration chooses the smallest eligible index for both the entering variable and the leaving variable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal simplex method for bounded variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau simplex for a bounded-variable minimization problem, with nonbasic variables maintained at lower or upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a basic feasible partition \([B,N_1,N_2]\), where \(x_{N_1}=\ell_{N_1}\) and \(x_{N_2}=u_{N_2}\), and form \(\widehat b=B^{-1}(b-N_1\ell_{N_1}-N_2u_{N_2})\) and \(\widehat z=c_BB^{-1}b+(c_{N_1}-c_BB^{-1}N_1)\ell_{N_1}+(c_{N_2}-c_BB^{-1}N_2)u_{N_2}\). If \(z_j-c_j\le0\) for every \(j\in N_1\) and \(z_j-c_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in N_2\), stop with the current solution optimal. Otherwise, increase a violating lower-bound variable or decrease a violating upper-bound variable by the step determined by the corresponding bounded-variable ratio test. If the permitted improving step is infinite, stop because the minimization objective is unbounded below; otherwise update the tableau and repeat, retaining lower- or upper-bound status flags for nonbasic variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a basic feasible solution and record whether each nonbasic variable is fixed at its lower or upper bound. The stated reduced-cost signs certify optimality. Increase a violating lower-bound variable or decrease a violating upper-bound variable using the appropriate bounded-variable ratio test. An infinite improving step certifies that the minimization problem is unbounded below; otherwise update the tableau and repeat.
assumptions_latex: \min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}
A=[B,N_1,N_2],\quad B\text{ is nonsingular}
x_{N_1}=\ell_{N_1},\quad x_{N_2}=u_{N_2},\quad \ell_B\le B^{-1}(b-N_1\ell_{N_1}-N_2u_{N_2})\le u_B
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[(z_j-c_j\le0\ \forall j\in N_1)\land(z_j-c_j\ge0\ \forall j\in N_2)\bigr]\Rightarrow x\text{ is optimal};\qquad \Delta_k=\infty\Rightarrow\inf c^Tx=-\infty.

knowledge_statements.title: General-Form Primal Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal simplex applied to mixed rows and general variable bounds through an equivalent equality representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a linear program with equality or inequality rows and interval-bounded or free variables, first apply exact row and variable transformations to obtain \(\min\{\tilde c^Tz:\tilde Az=\tilde b,\ z\ge0\}\). Construct a basis \(B\) with \(z_B=B^{-1}\tilde b\ge0\). At each iteration compute \(y=B^{-T}\tilde c_B\) and \(\bar c_N=\tilde c_N-\tilde A_N^Ty\). If \(\bar c_N\ge0\), return the inverse-transformed solution. Otherwise choose an index with negative reduced cost, apply the minimum-ratio test, and pivot; if no positive pivot coefficient exists, return the corresponding feasible recession direction as an unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transform the general LP to equality standard form, maintain primal feasibility, and use reduced costs, ratio tests, and an anti-cycling rule until optimality or certified unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: All row and variable transformations preserve feasibility and objective values up to a known constant.
The transformed constraint matrix has full row rank.
A primal-feasible initial basis is available.
A finite anti-cycling pivot rule is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates with an optimal general-form solution or a feasible recession direction proving unboundedness.

notation.meaning: variables in the transformed standard-form problem

children.title: General-Form Dual Simplex

knowledge_statements.title: General-Form Dual Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual simplex on an equivalent standard-form representation of a general linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Transform the general-form linear program exactly into \(\min\{\tilde c^Tz:\tilde Az=\tilde b,\ z\ge0\}\). Start with a basis \(B\) whose reduced costs \(\bar c_N=\tilde c_N-\tilde A_N^TB^{-T}\tilde c_B\) are nonnegative, although \(z_B=B^{-1}\tilde b\) may have negative components. Choose a row with negative basic value and perform a dual ratio-test pivot preserving \(\bar c_N\ge0\). Stop when \(z_B\ge0\), yielding an optimum, or when an infeasible row has no eligible entering column, yielding a Farkas infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After exact general-form transformations, dual simplex preserves reduced-cost feasibility while repairing negative basic values, ending with an optimum or infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The transformed constraint matrix has full row rank.
The initial basis is dual feasible.
An anti-cycling pivot rule is used when necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite termination yields either \(z_B\ge0\) with \(\bar c_N\ge0\), or a certificate that the primal constraints are infeasible.

children.title: Mixed-Sense Row Handling

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Sense Row Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equality-form representation of less-than, greater-than, and equality constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each mixed-sense row is converted independently. The row \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\) is represented by \(a_i^Tx+s_i=b_i\) with \(s_i\ge0\); the row \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) is represented by \(a_i^Tx-s_i=b_i\) with \(s_i\ge0\); and \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) is retained without a slack variable. Multiplying any row by \(-1\) reverses its inequality sense. These transformations preserve the feasible values of the original variables under projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a nonnegative slack to a less-than row, subtract one from a greater-than row, and retain equality rows unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projecting the equality-form feasible set onto \(x\) recovers exactly the original mixed-sense constraints.

notation.meaning: nonnegative slack or surplus variable for row i

knowledge_statements.title: Ranged-Row Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single bounded-slack representation of a finite two-sided linear row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite bounds \(L_i\le U_i\), the ranged row \(L_i\le a_i^Tx\le U_i\) is equivalent to the equality \(a_i^Tx+s_i=U_i\) together with \(0\le s_i\le U_i-L_i\). The correspondence is \(s_i=U_i-a_i^Tx\). If one endpoint is infinite, the row reduces to the corresponding one-sided inequality and uses an ordinary nonnegative slack or surplus variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sided row becomes one equality with a slack bounded between zero and the row width; infinite endpoints reduce to one-sided rows.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\).
The finite ranged-row bounds satisfy \(L_i\le U_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded-slack equality and the original ranged row define identical feasible values of \(x\).

notation.meaning: lower and upper activity bounds for row i

children.title: General Variable-Bound Handling
children.top_down_role: Simplex specialization for unrestricted, one-sided, or two-sided variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: General Variable-Bound Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form substitutions for lower-bounded, upper-bounded, boxed, fixed, and free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Variable domains admit exact substitutions. If \(l_j\le x_j\), set \(x_j=l_j+z_j\) with \(z_j\ge0\). If \(x_j\le u_j\), set \(x_j=u_j-z_j\) with \(z_j\ge0\). If \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\), use \(x_j=l_j+z_j\) with \(0\le z_j\le u_j-l_j\). If \(x_j\) is free, write \(x_j=z_j^+-z_j^-\) with \(z_j^+,z_j^-\ge0\). If \(l_j=u_j\), eliminate \(x_j\) by substitution. Objectives and right-hand sides are adjusted by the resulting constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift one-sided or boxed variables, split free variables into nonnegative parts, and eliminate fixed variables while adjusting constants.
assumptions_latex: Every stated finite bound is a real number.
For boxed variables, \(l_j\le u_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each substitution gives an exact correspondence between feasible original variables and feasible transformed variables, except for the nonunique split of a free variable.

notation.meaning: nonnegative parts representing a free variable

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Basis Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reoptimization initialized by a complete basis and nonbasic bound-status assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a modified bounded linear program \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), import a complete status assignment consisting of \(m\) proposed basic indices and a lower- or upper-bound status for every nonbasic index. Verify that the proposed basis matrix \(B\) is nonsingular, set nonbasic variables to their assigned bounds, and compute \(x_B=B^{-1}(b-A_Nx_N)\). Recompute reduced costs for the modified data. Start primal simplex if the reconstructed point is bound feasible, dual simplex if its reduced costs satisfy the bound-sign conditions, and otherwise run basis repair or feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete warm start imports every basis status, reconstructs basic values and reduced costs, then chooses primal, dual, or repair initialization.
assumptions_latex: The modified model retains compatible row and column identities.
The proposed basic set contains exactly \(m\) indices.
Every nonbasic variable has an admissible bound status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid imported assignment determines a unique reconstructed basic state for the modified problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Basis Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start construction from an incomplete set of proposed basic columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and a proposed basic index set \(P\) with \(|P|\le m\), discard unavailable indices and retain a maximal linearly independent subset of \(A_P\). Augment it with columns of \(A\), or with temporary artificial columns, until an invertible \(m\times m\) basis \(B\) is obtained. Assign admissible lower or upper statuses to remaining structural variables, compute the corresponding basic values, and pass the completed state to primal simplex, dual simplex, or a feasibility-restoration phase according to its feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate the proposed basic columns, augment them to a full nonsingular basis, assign remaining statuses, and select the appropriate simplex phase.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has row rank \(m\).
The supplied indices can be matched to columns of the current model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure either constructs a complete nonsingular starting basis containing the retained proposal or reports that the proposal cannot be reconciled under the allowed augmentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Completion of a partial independent column set is plausible, but the augmentation, artificial-column, status-assignment, and reconciliation rules are solver-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Partial Primal-Solution Starts

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Primal-Solution Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start construction from values supplied for only a subset of primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), let \(S\) index supplied estimates \(\hat x_S\). Clip finite-bound violations in \(\hat x_S\), initialize unspecified variables by admissible bound or crash rules, and obtain a completed estimate \(x^0\). Construct a basis-status assignment that seeks small constraint residual \(\|Ax^0-b\|\) while retaining the supplied values when compatible. Recompute the associated basic solution and reduced costs, then invoke primal simplex, dual simplex, or feasibility restoration according to the resulting feasibility conditions; the supplied values are hints, not constraints on the final optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete supplied primal values with admissible estimates, derive a basis-status assignment, and use feasibility tests to select the reoptimization phase.
assumptions_latex: The supplied variable identities match the current model.
All variable bounds are consistent.
A deterministic completion and crash rule is specified by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partial vector produces an initialization hint; it does not restrict the feasible set or require the optimizer to satisfy \(x_S=\hat x_S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Treating partial primal values as hints is reasonable, but clipping, completion, crash-basis construction, and residual minimization are implementation-dependent and lack a supporting source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Simplex Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start primal simplex for a modified finite-dimensional standard-form problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\). Input a basis index set \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that \(B=A_J\) is nonsingular and \(x_J=B^{-1}b\geq0\). Compute \(y=B^{-T}c_J\) and \(r_j=c_j-a_j^Ty\) for \(j\notin J\). While some \(r_j<0\), select an entering index using an anti-cycling pivot rule, set \(d=B^{-1}a_j\), and apply the minimum-ratio test over indices \(i\) with \(d_i>0\), using anti-cycling tie-breaking. If no such index exists, return the improving feasible ray \(p\) defined by \(p_j=1\), \(p_J=-d\), and \(p_k=0\) for all other nonbasic indices \(k\). Otherwise pivot and repeat. Stop when \(r_j\geq0\) for every \(j\notin J\), and return the resulting optimal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a primal-feasible basis, use anti-cycling primal-simplex pivots until all reduced costs are nonnegative; if an improving entering column has no limiting basic component, return its explicit unbounded ray.

\(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(|J|=m\), and \(B=A_J\) is nonsingular.

Form the candidate original active set from lifted basic variables, active bounds, and recovered row slacks. Select \(m=\operatorname{rank}(A)\) linearly independent columns to obtain \(B\). knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Mapping Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that a presolved basis need not determine a unique original basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min 0\) subject to \(x_1+x_2=1\) and \(x_1,x_2\ge 0\). If presolve aggregates the duplicate-role variables into \(y=x_1+x_2\), the presolved system is \(y=1\) with basis \(\{y\}\). In the original system, both \(B_1=[1]\), obtained by making \(x_1\) basic, and \(B_2=[1]\), obtained by making \(x_2\) basic, project to that same presolved basis. Thus aggregation loses the information needed for a unique inverse basis map; an explicit tie rule or basis reconstruction is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregating interchangeable columns makes distinct original bases project to one presolved basis, so postsolve cannot invert the basis map uniquely.
assumptions_latex: Presolve records the aggregate equation but not which interchangeable original column was basic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The presolved basis has no unique original-basis preimage.

Finally recompute primal values and reduced costs and reoptimize whenever feasibility or optimality is not retained.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with a primal- and dual-feasible basis matrix \(B\), and append \(a^Tx+s=\beta\) with a new slack \(s\ge0\) of zero objective coefficient. Retaining \(B\) and making \(s\) basic gives \[\widehat B=\begin{pmatrix}B&0\\a_B^T&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det(\widehat B)=\det(B)\ne0.\] Thus the extension is algebraically valid. At the inherited solution, the new basic value is \(s=\beta-a^Tx\), so the extended basis is primal feasible if and only if \(a^Tx\le\beta\). Assigning zero dual multiplier to the new row leaves every old reduced cost unchanged and gives the new slack reduced cost zero, so dual feasibility is inherited.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Reformulation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies structural master changes for which direct basis reuse is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A master basis may be transferred only when mapped basic columns form a square nonsingular matrix for the new row system and their induced basic values satisfy the new bounds. Likewise, replacing columns by aggregates without an invertible column-status map can destroy basis correspondence. Such reformulations require basis augmentation or reconstruction before simplex reoptimization, even when the previous primal solution can be embedded in the new formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stored warm start is algebraically valid when \(|B|=m\), \(A_B\) is nonsingular, \(B\cap N=\varnothing\), \(B\cup N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and each \(j\in N\) is fixed at its declared finite bound. Set \(x_B=A_B^{-1}(b-A_Nx_N)\), \(y=A_B^{-T}c_B\), and \(r=c-A^Ty\). It is primal feasible exactly when \(\ell_B\le x_B\le u_B\). It is dual feasible exactly when \(r_j\ge0\) for every lower-bound nonbasic variable and \(r_j\le0\) for every upper-bound nonbasic variable. If both tests hold, the basis is optimal for the current LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start requires a nonsingular full basis and valid nonbasic statuses; explicit basic-value and reduced-cost tests determine primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and optimality.
